subject: Clarify audit rights timing, pen-test notice & evidence runbook
messages:
From: Tim Winters <procurement@claritybio.com>

Cc: Laura Chen <security@claritybio.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:14:00 -0400
Subject: Clarify audit rights + pen-test timing for Order Form CLAR-2027-045

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo last week — ClarityBio is excited to move forward. Before we sign the Order Form we need to close a couple of security items with our InfoSec team: specifically the security exhibit language around audit rights and penetration testing.

Two quick asks from our side:
- Can you confirm the pen-test trigger language (who can initiate, whether customer tests are allowed, and any safety/coordination requirements)?
- We need an evidence cadence for SOC 2 artifacts (frequency, format, and a primary contact for evidence handoff).

I've attached our standard questionnaire (Clarity_Questionnaire_v1.pdf) that highlights the redlines we typically request. If possible, please point us to the part of the MSA/Order Form you intend to modify so we can route to our legal and security reviewers.

Tim Winters
Senior Procurement Manager, ClarityBio
procurement@claritybio.com

Attachment: Clarity_Questionnaire_v1.pdf
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Tim Winters <procurement@claritybio.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai, Laura Chen <security@claritybio.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify audit rights + pen-test timing for Order Form CLAR-2027-045

Tim — thanks, appreciate the clear list. Looping in Karthik (legal), Marissa (product/security liaison), and Connor (ops) so we can propose concrete language and a short evidence runbook.

Short answer up front: we can support SOC 2 artifact delivery and a mutually coordinated pen-test, but we suggest limiting live inspection to strictly scoped pen-tests with a 30-day notice and a non-destructive testing clause. Below is a proposed approach for the security exhibit though we still expect some legal redlines:

1) SOC 2 evidence cadence
- Annual SOC 2 Type II report delivered via secure link within 30 days of issuance.
- Quarterly snapshot of security posture: short summary (1p) + critical findings if any.
- Ad-hoc evidence: SAML/JWKS metadata, retention policy excerpts, and audit logs (sample sets) on request with 10 business days lead time.

2) Pen-test/inspection language (proposal)
- Pen-tests allowed with mutual written notice (>=30 days) and proof of insurance.
- Scope limited to customer-owned integration surface (customer-registered domains and API keys) and not internal-provider administrative infrastructure.
- Tests must be non-destructive and agreed in writing; Redwood will provide a staging endpoint where available.
- Redwood will not accept any scans that require privileged access to Redwood-managed infrastructure.

3) Evidence runbook (ops handoff)
- Primary handoff contact: security@redwood.ai (Marissa Co-lead); ops contact: connor_obrien@redwood.ai.
- Delivery methods: secure S3 link or encrypted Drive share; DocuSign/HubSpot references in contract for ordering.
- Typical turnaround: 10 business days for standard artifacts, 20 for logs/sample exports.

I'll attach a draft redline of the security exhibit that Karthik/legal can iterate on (redline-security-exhibit.docx). If that looks ok to you I'll ask Karthik to produce formal MSA/Order Form redlines for CLAR-2027-045.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Sales Engineering — Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

Attachments: redline-security-exhibit.docx
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Tim Winters <procurement@claritybio.com>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai, Laura Chen <security@claritybio.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 10:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify audit rights + pen-test timing for Order Form CLAR-2027-045

Tim / Vanessa — quick note from legal after looking at Vanessa's draft. High level: we are comfortable with the proposed cadence, with the following clarifications to preserve operational integrity and customer privacy.

Legal redline summary (highlights):
- Inspection rights: prefer providing SOC 2 Type II reports and attestation statements rather than unlimited live inspections. If live inspections are requested, they should be limited to discrete sampling windows and performed in a pre-agreed staging environment.
- Pen-test scope and responsibility: pen-tests that target Redwood-managed infrastructure will be explicitly prohibited; customer tests may target customer-configured workloads and tenant-level endpoints, subject to written scope approval.
- Notice period & remediation: 30-day notice for any customer-initiated pen-test; Redwood shall have a 10-business-day window to triage and remediate critical findings before public disclosure.
- Evidence requests: add a clause that mandates a single request point and a defined maximum frequency (e.g., no more than 4 ad-hoc requests per 12 months) unless mutually agreed.

Next steps: I will attach a tracked-change Order Form and MSA clause draft after one internal pass. Please confirm whether ClarityBio requires the ability to bring third-party testers (we can allow it with the same notice and indemnity requirements). Also confirm the preference for DocuSign vs. native e-sign flow for the final Order Form.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Attachment: security-exhibit-redlines.docx (legal tracked changes)
From: Tim Winters <procurement@claritybio.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: Laura Chen <security@claritybio.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify audit rights + pen-test timing for Order Form CLAR-2027-045

Thanks everyone — the approach looks reasonable and aligns with what our InfoSec team is comfortable with. A few clarifications from our side before we close: 

- Third-party testers: we plan to engage a contracted third-party for a tenant-level scan. We confirm they'll adhere to the same 30-day notice and carry standard cyber liability insurance.
- Non-destructive language: please add explicit language that tests will not perform data deletion or attempt privilege escalation beyond customer-scoped accounts.
- Evidence bounding: the 4-ad-hoc-requests-per-year cap is acceptable. For anything beyond that we'll route through the account owner to schedule.
- Signing flow: DocuSign is preferred; please include the Order Form ID CLAR-2027-045 on the DocuSign envelope so procurement can track internally.

Attached is a short PDF with our suggested redlines to the Order Form (proposed-orderform-redline.pdf). If Karthik can fold the agreed points into the contract and return a final tracked copy we can route internally for signature.

Regards,
Tim Winters
Senior Procurement Manager, ClarityBio
procurement@claritybio.com
